claims.text: The conventionally cast refractory HEA has coarse grains.
Alumina-forming elements are distributed inhomogeneously in the conventionally cast refractory HEA.
Switching from conventional casting to powder metallurgy with optimized sintering will produce a fine-grained microstructure.
Switching from conventional casting to powder metallurgy with optimized sintering will produce a more compositionally uniform microstructure.
Microstructural refinement will promote a uniform distribution of alumina-forming elements.
A uniform distribution of alumina-forming elements will enable formation of a protective oxide layer.
A refined and uniform microstructure will improve retention of the protective oxide layer.
A fine and homogeneous microstructure accelerates aluminum diffusion and oxidation kinetics.
Accelerated aluminum diffusion and oxidation promote formation of a continuous Al2O3 scale.
A continuous Al2O3 scale reduces further oxygen ingress.
Reduced oxygen ingress lowers oxidation-related weight gain.
After 100 hours at 1000°C in ambient air, the powder-metallurgy alloy will have lower weight gain than the cast alloy.
After the specified exposure, the powder-metallurgy alloy will have a more uniform oxide scale than the cast alloy.
After the specified exposure, the powder-metallurgy alloy will have a more adherent oxide scale than the cast alloy.
The proposed improvement is expected only for high-temperature oxidation in ambient air and may not transfer to other atmospheres or temperature regimes.
Failure to obtain at least a 10% reduction in weight gain together with improved oxide-scale uniformity would falsify the hypothesis.
